clue.text: South American soldier assigned to war-torn Guyana

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

indicators.note: torn apart by war, so the letters of the country's name are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier from the continent is posted to a Guyana ravaged by conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'war-torn' reads as scene-setting for Guyana but is the anagram signal, giving GUAYAN; 'assigned to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Paraguay is a South American, used here as a noun.

clue.text: Advance, making way through mountain

definitions.meaning: an advance or ... is an amorous approach, as in 'make a ...'

explanation.definitionFit: A pass is both a romantic advance and a gap or route through a mountain range.

clue.text: Swimmer looking embarrassed with dated hairstyle

parts.note: red, as in red-faced, means embarrassed
the mullet, short at front and long at back, was a 1980s haircut

explanation.surface: A bather looks red-faced about their old-fashioned haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A red mullet is a fish, so a swimmer in crossword terms.

clue.text: Make extra special effort? Get lost!

definitions.meaning: to take more trouble than needed to help
a rude instruction to move aside, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to take extra trouble, and literally a command to clear off from one's path.

clue.text: Nasty illness: worker taken to hospital, having mentioned pains

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: mentioned means the word is spoken, so we take its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: racks are torments or pains

explanation.surface: A labourer ends up in hospital with a horrible disease, complaining of aches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mentioned' turns RACKS into its sound-alike RAX; 'taken to' and 'having' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthrax is a serious bacterial disease of livestock and people.

clue.text: In American editions name is changed

indicators.note: In tells us the name letter goes inside one of the edition abbreviations

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for edition; the plural gives two of them
the second of the two edition abbreviations

explanation.surface: In the US versions of a book, a character's name has been altered.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'editions' supplies two edition abbreviations; 'In' puts the name letter inside the first. 'In American editions' looks like scene-setting, not wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Amended means altered or revised, a synonym of changed.

clue.text: Almost the whole of Australia rejected European writer

indicators.note: rejected signals that the assembled letters are turned back to front
almost signals that the last letter of the word for the whole is dropped

parts.note: the whole means all
Oz is the familiar name for Australia

explanation.surface: Australia, nearly in its entirety, has spurned an author from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims ALL to AL; AL + OZ is read backwards because of 'rejected'.
explanation.definitionFit: Emile Zola was the French novelist of the Rougon-Macquart cycle, so a European author.

clue.text: Tree is healthier when lopped

indicators.note: lopped means cut off at the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: rosier, of cheeks, means healthier looking

explanation.surface: A tree is in better shape after it has been pruned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when lopped' takes the first letter off ROSIER; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a willow, used for basket weaving.

clue.text: Adult goes regularly at speed over a motorway abroad

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter is taken from the two words
over means the word for speed is turned round

parts.note: to dart is to speed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grown-up keeps driving fast over a foreign highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the word for speed to give TRAD. 'at' is a link meaning next to; the blog's commenters found that use of 'at' fiendish.
explanation.definitionFit: An autostrada is an Italian motorway, so a motorway abroad for a British solver.

clue.text: Cook can triple wages in seaside resorts

indicators.note: to cook figures is to fiddle them, so the letters are falsified into a new order

explanation.surface: A chef can earn three times the pay in a holiday town by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges CAN TRIPLE WAGES; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Watering places is an old name for spas and seaside holiday towns.

clue.text: Assumed one's ignored at party?

indicators.note: ignored tells us the letter for one is not counted in the word

parts.note: said, as in 'the said person', means supposed or taken as given
one is the Roman numeral I; 'one's ignored' means that I is left out
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone takes it for granted that they will be left standing alone at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' removes the I, leaving SAD; 'at' is a link. Read whole, the clue also pictures the wallflower, though the blog's commenters doubted the &lit reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddo is British slang for a pathetic, socially inept person, the kind left alone at parties.

clue.text: Medical practitioner, the first to introduce charge

indicators.note: the first two pieces take the word for charge into the gap between them

parts.note: taken as written
1st written with I for the figure 1
a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'take the rap'

explanation.surface: A doctor, the first one in line to bring in a fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is written 1ST, the figure read as the letter I, a common crossword trick; 'to introduce' takes the charge into the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist treats patients, so is a kind of medical practitioner.

clue.text: Refined noble wearing extremely precious jewels

parts.note: refined, of a person's taste, means cultured

indicators.note: the nobleman wears those letters around him like clothing
extremely points to the outermost letters, first and last, of the next word

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A sophisticated aristocrat dons some very costly jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives P and S, the first and last letters of 'precious'; 'wearing' puts EARL inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Cultured pearls are grown in farmed oysters and worn as jewels.

clue.text: Kind of fish one made available where food is served

parts.note: char is a fish related to trout
I is the Roman numeral for one
food is served at the table

explanation.surface: A sort of fish is put on offer in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of fish' looks like the definition, but 'Kind' alone is. 'made available' is a link, food on a table being available; commenters on the blog found it weak.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable means generous and kind to others.

clue.text: Prince I send document to in northern location

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's name for the young Henry V
to fax someone is to send them a document by telephone line

explanation.surface: A royal personage says he will fax over a document to someone in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: HALIFAX is a town in West Yorkshire, in the north of England; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Halifax is a Yorkshire town, so a place in northern England.

clue.text: Dispute between duke and monarch makes one unsettled

indicators.note: between places the word for dispute in the middle of the other two pieces

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
a rift is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: A quarrel between a duke and the sovereign leaves someone feeling insecure.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword monarch; 'between' places the dispute in the middle of duke and monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter is a person with no settled home or job.

clue.text: Pointed at short student teacher

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a trainee is someone learning a job
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A pupil teacher, briefly, was singled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' takes the final E off TRAINEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Trained on means aimed or directed at, as a gun or camera is.

clue.text: In outskirts of Redbridge, turning to join train

indicators.note: In places the turned word inside the outer letters
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters
turning means the word for join is read backwards

parts.note: to join is to unite

explanation.surface: On the edge of Redbridge, a London borough, someone turns to board a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' gives R and E from 'Redbridge'; 'turning' makes ETINU, and 'In' places it between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the train of attendants following an important person.

clue.text: On the way to Paris?

parts.note: the French phrase for 'on the way', fit for a Parisian, rather than travelling towards the city

explanation.definitionFit: En route is French for on the way, borrowed into English.

clue.text: Orchestra's attempt to overcome grand embargo

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: to overcome is to sit over and around, so the attempt surrounds the rest

parts.note: a bid is an attempt
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
a ban is an embargo

explanation.surface: An orchestra tries to get round a ban costing a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' looks like an adjective for the embargo but is the letter G; 'to overcome' has the attempt surround the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A big band is a large jazz or swing orchestra.

clue.text: Being bad, no heart to eat fried snack

indicators.note: bad signals the letters of the word are spoilt into a new order
no heart says the middle letter is taken out

explanation.surface: Feeling unwell, someone has no stomach to eat a fried treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges BEING to BEIGN; 'no heart' removes A from EAT, leaving ET. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A beignet is a fritter or doughnut, fried in batter.

clue.text: Book revealing a certain girl's name is in vogue

indicators.note: is in tells us the preceding pieces go inside the word for vogue

parts.note: a trend is a vogue or fashion
sure means certain
Isla is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A book discloses that a particular girl's name has become fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a certain girl' looks like one person but is three pieces; 'is in' puts them inside the word for vogue, and 'revealing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure Island is Robert Louis Stevenson's pirate novel.

clue.text: Measures taken to confine one who wrote sexy books?

indicators.note: the measures are made to hold the letter for one inside them

parts.note: ells are old measures of cloth length
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Steps are taken to lock up an author of erotic fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Havelock Ellis wrote serious studies of sexual psychology, hence the question mark on 'sexy books'.
explanation.definitionFit: Havelock Ellis was an author of studies on human sexuality.

clue.text: Player felt two central points had been lost

indicators.note: had been lost says those letters are taken out

parts.note: sensed means felt
N and S are compass points, here also the middle letters of the word for felt

explanation.surface: A sportsman sensed that a couple of key points had slipped away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had been lost' removes N and S from the middle of SENSED. A seed is a ranked tennis player.
explanation.definitionFit: A seed is a player ranked in a tournament draw to keep top players apart.

clue.text: Plain St Thomas refusing a second altar canopy

parts.note: bald means plain or unadorned, as in a bald statement

indicators.note: refusing means the saint's name turns away the following letters

parts.note: St Thomas Aquinas, the medieval theologian

explanation.surface: A simple saint Thomas declines a moment's pause beneath an altar canopy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refusing' drops the A and the S for second from the saint's surname, leaving AQUIN; 'St Thomas' points to the theologian Aquinas, not the apostle.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldaquin is an ornamental canopy over an altar or throne.

clue.text: King captured by rebel group

indicators.note: captured by means the king letter is held inside the rebel's name

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion in 1450
R, for Rex, means king

explanation.surface: A monarch is taken prisoner by a band of insurgents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured by' puts R inside CADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a small group of trained activists or officers.

clue.text: Language used by Peter Sellers

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The comic actor Peter Sellers had a way of speaking all his own.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic, a language.

clue.text: Boy in plane bound to be thrown out

parts.note: a jet is a plane

indicators.note: in places the boy inside the word for bound

parts.note: bound means tied
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad on an aircraft is sure to get ejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the boy inside the word for bound; 'to be' is a link. 'plane bound' reads as one idea in the surface but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Jettisoned means discarded, cast overboard or thrown out.
